checks.message: primary image cap would be exceeded

monitored: GPU: wall-clock x allocated devices from launch to confirmed process-tree termination
RSS: psutil sum over the launched process tree, every 5 s; aggregate over all live jobs; supervisor kills the tree above 120 GiB aggregate (cap 128 GiB)
CPU: max(psutil process-tree cpu_times incl. reaped children, wait4 rusage of the direct child)
threads: sampled process-tree num_threads, peak recorded (advisory; BLAS/OMP worker count is enforced only by OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2 per job and <=4 concurrent jobs)
storage: `du -sb` of the task root every 120 s while jobs run; growth vs. first sample recorded; free space on /data polled every 5 s (kill below 50 GiB)
images: reserved before launch, actual decodes from per-job append-only decode counters
gaps: Storage is polled at 120 s granularity and only for the task root; transient spikes between polls and files written outside the root (TMPDIR/XDG caches on /data) are not attributed. Reported storage peaks are lower bounds, not exact compliance claims.
CPU core-hours exclude CPU used by processes that escaped the launched session and were not descendants at a sampling instant; reported CPU is a lower bound.
Thread count is not a BLAS-worker count; the 8-worker aggregate is enforced by launch-time reservation of declared workers (2/job) plus env thread limits, not by cgroup.
GPU memory (40 GB/device) is not monitored by the supervisor; OOM surfaces as a child failure and is charged like any failure.
RSS counts resident file-backed mapped pages (safetensors mmap) as RSS; this overstates the private footprint (conservative for the cap).
Other users' processes on the same machine are invisible to the accounting except through the pre-launch foreign-process probe on the requested devices.
If the supervisor is killed uncleanly, children whose end time was unobserved are charged at their full reservation (conservative over-charge, flagged).
